findings.reason: the node cannot edit the tests its own deliverable tells it to change without a scope grant, so the plan must add those test files to §1's write paths (or restore the widen clause).
findings.text: §1's write paths grant only recovery_review_delivery.py, recovery_review_dispatch.py, recovery_review_acceptance.py and the new tests/test_a_review_promotes_only_its_own_verdict.py, yet the deliverable requires changing the existing tests that "relied on the legacy path counting as a delivery" — tests/test_a_review_run_promotes_itself.py (write_paths=[legacy review_path] at line 147) and tests/test_a_delivered_review_ends_its_turn.py (write_paths=[legacy review_path] at line 139) — neither of which is in scope, and the "added to the scope with crew widen" clause present in the prior revision of this line has been removed

findings.reason: leaving them red satisfies item 5 only by naming them, which contradicts the deliverable's instruction to change the tests that encoded the defect; the plan must either scope the edits or state that these two tests are expected to stay red.
findings.text: done-when item 5 runs tests/test_a_review_run_promotes_itself.py and tests/test_a_delivered_review_ends_its_turn.py and requires "no failure against the base, beyond the tests the manifest names as encoding the defect", but under §1's four conditions those two tests FAIL at the fixed revision (each stores its record at the legacy review_path(...) and declares write_paths=[that legacy path], so _delivered_review_record now returns None and self-promotion is refused)
